Am I understanding correctly that the aim of this change is to make it so that when a new EM config is added to configurations/, the submitter would run generate_config_list.sh, then commit the updates configurations/meson.build along with their changes-- instead of just updating the existing meson.build like we'd do today?


When you say

> There is a tradeoff when running a command to get the filenames, as it
may not regenerate when file is added/removed

That sounds like a potentially serious tradeoff if we're replacing the existing list (relatively easy for change submitters to maintain, IMO) with a file that has '# This file is auto-generated. Do not edit manually.' at the top.

What situations would result in the script *not* updating the list when a config is added or removed?

yes, the idea is that the list is a separate file and not updated manually.

>What situations would result in the script not updating the list when a config is added or removed?

As long as you run the script, it should be fine. I initially wanted to avoid the script and just use 'find'to get all the filenames but came across that meson documentation as to why all the files are explicitly mentioned.

That sounds like it makes sense to me.

Assuming Entity-Manager maintainers have don't have other objections, I think it'd make sense to make a revision that also updates the Entity-Manager readme to mention this script should be run after adding or changing the name of an entity-manager config.

...And maybe not worth the effort to dig in too deep for now (let's see what other folks think)-- but I wonder if it could make sense to have a script like this run as part of the automatic CI tests processes that get called before/when submitting new changes for Entity-Manager to Gerrit.

It's a simple thing to fix, but I know I've definitely submitted config files in the past without remembering to update the meson.build first

> Assuming Entity-Manager maintainers have don't have other objections, I think it'd make sense to make a revision that also updates the Entity-Manager readme to mention this script should be run after adding or changing the name of an entity-manager config.

Many people don't read documentation. It tends to be outdated anyways.
But you are right that it should be clear how to update this file.

This is fixed in the latest revision. The script now puts its own filename
into the generated file. So it is clear how the file is generated.

> It's a simple thing to fix, but I know I've definitely submitted config files in the past without remembering to update the meson.build first

Same. But i would prefer to keep this change simple and just focus on automating the process of creating that list.

>Many people don't read documentation. It tends to be outdated anyways.
But you are right that it should be clear how to update this file.

I hear ya on that-- but the contents of the readme.md are displayed on the front page of openbmc/entity-manager and is likely to be looked over by anyone looking to add a new configuration.

I think it'd make sense to add a bit to the end of the readme that explains that this script should be called anytime a new configuration is added, removed, or renamed to update a list meson is relying on.

>The script now puts its own filename into the generated file.

by 'generated file' are you referring to the configuration/meson.build file you uploaded with the new list of configs? If so, based on the changes between rev 3 and rev 5, I'm suspecting you meant to remove the configuration/meson.build and replace it with another file that didn't get added to the most recent commit.

That's just a guess on my end.

>Same. But i would prefer to keep this change simple and just focus on automating the process of creating that list

Very understandable. Honestly, I would have thought someone else with a 'strong opinion' would have chimed in on this topic by now.

I think it might be a good idea for you to go to the openbmc Discord -- maybe under the 'Inventory' channel, then post a list to this PR with a brief description and see if any folks have 'opinions' on this topic that just didn't see this review yet.

> I think it'd make sense to add a bit to the end of the readme that explains that this script should be called anytime a new configuration is added, removed, or renamed to update a list meson is relying on.

Added the documentation as requested 👍

+1 on the general idea of not needing to manually update the list of configuration files in the Entity-Manager meson.build, tho I'm sure more experience folks will have strong opinions about implementation if this goes forward...
Ideally you would add something to the CI script that also attempts to regenerate so we fail if someone didn't update.
Done
We should do something to remove the ./ here
Done
Need a sort here to ensure stability.
Done
nit: 4 spaces. I think meson format would change this for you. We should generate with something stable under meson format.
Done. Checked with meson format that there is no diff.
I think you can just rerun the script and any diffs at the end will automatically fail?  Happens the same as our formatting.

Probably, but then it will not fail anymore when running the plain script locally.

It's only one extra line to make it explicit what is happening without having to know about the details how CI works.

I guess PDI does do a check. You should use git calls though rather than copying/raw diff. 

https://github.com/openbmc/phosphor-dbus-interfaces/blob/7f154004885f4e98bd8d0aa6f66259c117b95a4c/gen/run-ci#L6
Done
this link recommends using run_command to explicitly run the script.  Any reason we avoided that here?

The overhead. There is no need to run the command for each build.

The file only needs to be regenerated when config is added/moved/removed.

The reference talks in detail about how incremental builds with meson + ninja are efficient because every dependency of a target is listed and there are no wildcards.

If you use wildcards, things need to run each time you do an incremental build.

> The overhead.

we're talking about a command that runs in sub second time during a 10+ second operation..... Are we effecting the configure time in a measurable way?


It seems a little odd that we link the meson maintainers recommendations for this, then don't follow their recommendations.  I agree about wildcards, but don't understand why we're avoiding run_command, which is what that link recommends.

The time for meson to reconfigure itself is around 5 seconds for me.

So if we are running the script each time that's 5 seconds extra for every build. 

I would be interested to see a patch if someone finds a more clever way to do this.
LGTM, will wait for other maintainers to weigh in.
How long do we wait? People had 2 weeks to comment on this simple patch 😞
As long as it takes.  Feel free to add yourself to the reviewers list and start reviewing patches if you believe it takes too long.

I'm not sure how much we need to care, but this is going to break every fork that ever added an EM config.  I'm fine to do that, but lets not do it lightly, and lets make sure we get the output right so we only have to break everyone once.

Here's an example of how people typically do this.
There is no need to create a patch or fork to add a configuration.
```
     install -d ${D}${datadir}/entity-manager/configurations
     install -m 0444 ${UNPACKDIR}/ethanolx-baseboard.json ${D}${datadir}/entity-manager/configurations
```

If there is a list of supported forks, where is this documented?
Do we need to create a pull request on that fork in that case?

sure 👍

https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/entity-manager/+/77352

> If there is a list of supported forks, where is this documented?

We don't support forks officially.  Some do it the way you've done it.  Some just fork entity-manager which would be effected by this change.  Like I said, we don't have to care, but lets make sure this solves the problem so we're not doing this more than once in a short period of time.
Acknowledged

The main readme seems like the wrong place for this.

maybe in CONFIG_FORMAT.md, that specifically talks about the configuration files?
makes sense. Moved it there 👍

Should this generation be part of something like auto_json, which is already known and run by developers?  Creating a new script that devs now have to know exists adds roadblocks (albiet minor ones).  What were the motivations for a new script vs using an existing?

Alternatively, could validate_configs just check to see if a config is missing?

Which roadblock? Just run the script. It's been documented.

> Alternatively, could validate_configs just check to see if a config is missing?

That's an overhead each time that is run. Which is not needed.

> Which roadblock? Just run the script. It's been documented.
> 

You have to know the documentation and script exist;  It's less of a roadblock if the "normal" flow just works correctly, which would be my preference if there's not a good technical reason to avoid it.

> > Alternatively, could validate_configs just check to see if a config is missing?
> 
> That's an overhead each time that is run. Which is not needed.

This is the second time you've mentioned overhead, and I don't really understand what you mean by it.  That script already opens every file and parses them fully.  The overhead in also writing out a new meson file is likely unmeasurable.

> You have to know the documentation and script exist; It's less of a roadblock if the "normal" flow just works correctly, which would be my preference if there's not a good technical reason to avoid it.

There is a trail of comments guiding people to the script. Even in the output of the script itself. I would be surprised if folks used to the old flow would not find it.

I think we should get this in and then tweak it from there if people want to contribute improvements of workflow.  The important thing is that we're getting coverage in CI, which this does.  Anything else is just a cherry on top to me.

(I'm tired of asking for sorting of the meson.build in code reviews)
yea let's just get this in.
Seems like I didn't respond fast enough.  Oh well, I guess if everyone else thinks this is an improvement I'm ok with it.
